targetWords.definition: Actually means in fact or really.
targetWords.example: ■My dad looks a little mean, but actually he's very kind.

targetWords.definition: Bite is the act of using your teeth to cut and tear into something.
targetWords.example: The boy took a big bite out of his hamburger.

targetWords.definition: The coast is the land by an ocean.
targetWords.example: ■I stayed on the southern coast ofAustralia.

targetWords.definition: A deal is an agreement that you have with another person.
targetWords.example: I made a deal with the other company to give us some money.

targetWords.definition: The desert is an area of land without many plants or water.
targetWords.example: Not many plants grow in the desert.

targetWords.definition: An earthquake is a shaking movement of the ground.
targetWords.example: The building shook during the earthquake.

targetWords.definition: If something is effective, it works well.
targetWords.example: Swimming is an effective way to stay healthy.

targetWords.definition: To examine something is to look at it carefully.
targetWords.example: The doctor examined my eyes today.

targetWords.definition: If something is false, it is not correct.
targetWords.example: If you think the answer is false, press the red button.

targetWords.definition: A gift is something you give someone.
Hunger is the feeling that you get when you need to eat.
targetWords.example: •After playing all day long, he was filled with hunger.

targetWords.definition: To imagine something is to think of it in your mind.
targetWords.example: Sally imagined herself winning lots of money.

targetWords.definition: A journey is a long trip.
targetWords.example: I went on a journey across the country with my parents.

targetWords.definition: A puzzle is something that is hard to understand.
targetWords.example: The question was a puzzle to him.

targetWords.definition: Quite is used to say that something is complete or very much.
targetWords.example: ■I think typing on a keyboard is quite easy.

targetWords.definition: Rather is used when you want to do one thing but not the other.
targetWords.example: I would rather have the red one than the blue one.

targetWords.definition: If something is specific, it is precise or exact.
targetWords.example: ■Please choose a specific place on the map.

targetWords.definition: A tour is a short trip in which you see many sights.
targetWords.example: I took a tour ofAsia and Europe.

targetWords.definition: —•Ken took a trip to the city yesterday.
If something has value, it is worth a lot of money. Matthew found a treasure of very high value.

story.title: The Spider and the Bird
story.passage:
There was once a very big spider. If a bug got into his web, he would examine

it. However, he didn't eat the bug right away. He asked the bug a question first. It

was always quite a difficult puzzle. If the bug's answer was correct, he let it go. If

not, he ate it.

One day, a small bird on a journey flew into the spider's web. The spider

couldn't imagine eating a bird. It was so big! But his hunger was too great. He

said to the bird, " If you cannot give me a specific answer, I will eat you."

The bird laughed. " I could eat you!" But the bird was actually scared. She had

used all her energy trying to get out of the web. And a spider's bite can be very

effective in killing animals.

" Please don't eat me," the bird said. " I would rather make a deal with you."

" OK," the spider said. " If your answer is right, I will let you go. If not, you must

give me a gift. It must be something of great value."

The bird said, "You can pick anything you want to eat. I will find it for you." The

spider agreed.

"Where can you take a trip to the coast, the desert, and the mountains at the

same time?" the spider asked.

The bird asked, " Does this place have earthquakes?" But the spider did not

say anything. " I can see those places when I fly. Is the 'sky' the right answer?"

" False!" said the spider. "The answer is Hawaii! Now you must find some bugs

for me."

The spider climbed on the bird's back.

They flew and ate bugs together. They

took a tour

of the

forest.

the bird took

the spider home.

From that day on,

they were friends.

And they never

tried to eat each other

again.
